label: Today You Will Learn
h: The difference between what is accurate and what deserves your sustained attention, and a six-question test to decide.
body:
About 8 minutes, plus one short pause · one small practice · no homework list

Scrolling that is hard to control or disrupts sleep deserves assessment, not more willpower. Persistent low mood, or vivid images and nightmares tied to something you experienced, are reasons to speak with a professional.

label: Key Scripture
h: "Whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence, if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things."

label: Meet Andrew
h: "Everything I read is probably true. I am not reading lies. So why does it feel like poison?"
body: Two or three hours every evening. Could not say what had actually happened to interest rates.

label: The Main Truth · Accurate Is Not The Only Question
body:
Accurate but incompleteThe ordinary and the good removed from the picture.
Accurate but unresolvedA prediction is not yet a fact.
Accurate but nothing to doResponsibility without the possibility of action.
Accurate but built for alarmArranged around urgency, not proportion.
Accurate, plus a claim about God"He has withdrawn." "He is a spectator."

label: A Common Belief
h: "Philippians 4:8 means Christians should only think about nice things."
body: If it forbade thinking about hard things, Paul broke it three chapters earlier. The right reading is neither "only nice things" nor "anything at all".

label: The Tool · Six Questions For Anything You Dwell On
body:
Established?Fact, interpretation, prediction or opinion?
Proportionate?Fair to the wider picture?
Worthy?Honourable, or built to provoke?
Relevant?Does dwelling serve anything?
Honest about God?Have I attached a claim he has not made?
Bounded?A minute, a morning, or every evening?

label: The Mind Is Fed From Two Directions
body:
What you take inScreens, conversations, sources. Run the test on the two or three that occupy you most.
What you generatePredictions, replays, rehearsals, mind-readings. Run the same test.

Andrew did not stop reading the news. He stopped reading forecasts of it.

label: What To Dwell On Instead
body:
ScriptureThe people in front of youThe work that is yoursThe good present in your dayThe character of God

It will feel at first like a poorer diet than alarm, because alarm is stimulating. It is not poorer.

label: Do This Now
h: Name one source that repeatedly alarms you without improving your understanding. Write what you will do with it tomorrow: pause it, or set a limit.
body:
Then write what you will give that time to instead. Not information you need for work, safety or a deadline.

Pause the audio

h: Not everything true deserves an evening.

label: Prayer
body:
Father, you know what I have been feeding my mind.

Teach me to know what needs knowing once,
and to let it go.

Fill the space with what is true and worthy,
and with you.

Amen.
